item.title: Topological and measurewise amenability for locally compact groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2611.10010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the equivalence of topological and measurewise amenability for $\sigma$-compact locally compact groupoids with a Hausdorff unit space and a continuous Haar system. This in particular includes the second countable locally compact Hausdorff case. Our proof averages arbitrary Radon probability measures along strictly positive densities to obtain quasi-invariant measures. We overcome the lack of absolute continuity of the original measure with respect to its quasi-invariant substitute by also averaging the Reiter functions along the same density.
item.dc:creator: Julian Kranz

item.title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
item.description: arXiv:2611.10387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $\alpha$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $\alpha> 1/2$ and for the case $\alpha=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Panja, Diptesh Saha

item.title: Solid factors associated to the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Set $\Gamma_n=SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (respectively $PSL_2(\mathbb{Z})$) for $n$ even (respectively for $n$ odd). Then $\Gamma_n$ acts on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ through the restriction of the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that that the von Neumann algebra $L(\mathbb{Z}^n\rtimes \Gamma_n)$ is a solid factor. This generalizes the case $n=2$ proved by N. Ozawa.
item.dc:creator: Paul Jolissaint

item.title: Differences Between Quantum Symmetries of Graphs and Graph $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.11417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish several characteristic differences between the quantum symmetry groups of directed graphs and their associated graph $C^*$-algebras in the frameworks of Banica and Joardar-Mandal, respectively, considering the family of finite directed graphs without isolated vertices and without multiple edges.
item.dc:creator: Ujjal Karmakar, Arnab Mandal

item.title: An invariant higher index pairing under Morita equivalence for proper \'etale groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2611.11982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For suitable proper \'etale groupoids, we study a part of the higher index that is invariant under Morita equivalence. We capture this part by a pairing between cyclic homology classes associated with isotropy groups and cyclic cohomology classes of the groupoid convolution algebra. We show that the pushforward is compatible with the maps induced by essential equivalences. This gives a numerical invariant depending only on the Morita equivalence class of the groupoid. In the case of a finite group action, we relate the resulting pairing to the equivariant index and to the Atiyah-Bott fixed-point formula.
item.dc:creator: Yu Qiao, Bing Kwan So, Hang Wang

item.title: Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.12498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.
item.dc:creator: Trung Hoa Dinh

item.title: The space of Dimension functions on a $C^*$-algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.12518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the space of normalized dimension functions on a unital $C^*$-algebra is either empty or a Choquet simplex. As a byproduct, we show that $W(A)$ is hereditary in $\operatorname{Cu}(A)$ for every $C^*$-algebra $A$. The argument combines an exact factorization for Cuntz comparison with Birkhoff's decomposition of lattice valuations. Moreover, we show that the space of normalized rank functions on a unital ring is either empty or a Choquet simplex.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Liu, Tao Zhang

item.title: Positivity Improving Quantum Markov Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.10042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Markov operator on a matrix algebra, that is, a unital completely positive map, is called positivity improving if it maps every nonzero positive element to an invertible one. This is the noncommutative counterpart of a stochastic matrix with strictly positive entries. We show that positivity improvement is self-dual and equivalent to a faithful quantum Markov--Dobrushin--Doeblin minorization. We also compare the scalar trace minorization with the optimal common-lower-bound construction of the quantum Markov--Dobrushin coefficient. We then characterize positivity improvement through the Kraus space of the map: a Markov operator is positivity improving if and only if the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal complement of its Kraus space contains no operator of rank one. As a consequence the Kraus rank of a positivity improving Markov operator on the algebra of $d\times d$ matrices is at least $2d-1$, and an explicit Hankel-type channel shows that this bound is attained in every dimension. Although deciding positivity improvement is NP-hard in general, we obtain complete and effectively checkable classifications for qubits and qutrits, together with families of examples (Pauli, Weyl and Werner--Holevo channels) showing that all our estimates are optimal. Finally we show that, in infinite dimensions, positivity improvement no longer implies any contraction of the Markov operator.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Accardi, Abdessatar Souissi

item.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.10159v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.
item.dc:creator: A. Yu. Savin, K. N. Zhuikov

item.title: A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.10299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|\chi_u+\chi_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.
item.dc:creator: Yoonje Jeong, Sang-Gyun Youn

item.title: A trace costs one quantifier: the exact complexity of perfect play in nonlocal games
item.description: arXiv:2611.10481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a finite nonlocal game, can the players win with certainty? We prove that the existence of a perfect normal spatial strategy is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete, even when restricted to games of value one, so it cannot be decided even with an oracle for the halting problem. This is strictly harder than perfect play in the finite-dimensional and commuting-operator models, which are $\Sigma^0_1$-complete and $\Pi^0_1$-complete. Within the commuting model, the existence of a perfect normal strategy with a finite or semifinite von Neumann host is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete, whereas for every fixed type $\mathrm{III}_\lambda$ subtype it has the same $\Pi^0_1$-complete language as unrestricted commuting play. A trace thus costs one existential number quantifier: the hardness constructions force every perfect strategy to choose a finite clock period or a finite tree depth. Spatial $\Sigma^0_2$-completeness also holds when finite entanglement entropy is required, and both forms are formally verified in Lean. For every computable $0<\alpha<1$, perfect spatial play with $\mathrm{Tr}\,h^\alpha<\infty$ for the reduced density $h$ is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete as well; these conditions form a strict ladder between finite rank and finite entropy. We also prove $\Sigma^0_2$-completeness for one-shot zero-error communication with normal entanglement, and construct a finite channel with zero-error codes of a given size each of which needs infinite entanglement entropy.
item.dc:creator: Seth Douglas, Nidhal Mghirbi

item.title: On S\l oci\'nski-type decomposition, BCL model and unitary extension of commuting Banach space Wold isometries
item.description: arXiv:2611.11536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The adjoint of an operator plays the central role in Hilbert space operator theory. In particular, dilations of Hilbert space contractions, extension of commuting Hilbert space isometries to Hilbert space unitaries, orthogonal decompositions of contractions and functional models for commuting isometries are heavily dependent on the presence of adjoint. In this paper, we develop a theory of Banach space Wold isometries with right-complemented ranges by showing explicit constructions of Berger-Coburn-Lebow model and unitary extension for such isometric tuple without the help of adjoint. We also show that a S\l oci\'nski type decomposition is possible for such a commuting tuple of Banach space isometries. Each of our results generalizes the corresponding result in the Hilbert space theory.
item.dc:creator: Swapan Jana, Sourav Pal, Saikat Roy

item.title: Transformations of Hilbert Module Reference Frames
item.description: arXiv:2611.11683v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we provide a functorial characterization of Hilbert module classical and quantum reference frames. Using the functorial characterization, we construct a category for equivariant couplings and Hilbert module reference frames. We prove the construction of the reference frame system from the equivariant coupling data yields a functor. We also deduce a ``unitary" groupoid as frame transformations for Hilbert module reference frames of a fixed Hilbert module dynamical system. We provide some examples of these frame transformations in the case of the indistinguishable classical two state switch and in the case of Hilbert spaces.
item.dc:creator: Lucus Brady

item.title: Eccentricity in mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthographs of C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.11703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the eccentricity of every vertex in the orthograph of mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthogonality for arbitrary finite-dimensional C*-algebras and for the algebra K(H) of compact operators on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. This gives a more detailed description of the orthograph introduced by Aramba\v{s}i\'c et al. (Banach J. Math. Anal. 14 (2020), 1751-1772). As an application, we characterize scalar multiples of unitary elements among invertible elements of finite-dimensional C*-algebras in terms of eccentricity alone. We also show that M_3(C) is the only finite-dimensional C*-algebra whose orthograph has a non-trivial connected component of radius 3.
item.dc:creator: Srdjan Stefanovi\'c

item.title: An optimal quantum strategy for the $2$-hat game
item.description: arXiv:2611.11759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the two-player hat game as a two-input, three-output non-local game. We calculate the quantum commuting value and show that it coincides with the quantum one. In particular, we show that \[\omega_{\rm q}(H_2)=\omega_{\mathrm{qc}}(H_2)=\frac{15+\sqrt{33}}{36}\approx 0.576238.\] We achieve the optimal quantum advantage using a shared non-maximally entangled qutrit state. To establish optimality, we exploit the game's symmetry under the dihedral group $D_8$ and apply its representation theory to substantially reduce the complexity of the underlying matrix problem. We also determine the no-signalling value $\omega_{\mathrm{ns}}(H_2)=2/3$.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Baziotis, Sang-Jun Park, Sang-Gyun Youn

item.title: Proof of the R\'{e}nyi QNEC
item.description: arXiv:2611.11760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a general proof of the R\'{e}nyi QNEC formulated using the Araki-Masuda weighted $L_p$ norms for all $p > 2$. This generalizes the algebraic proof of the QNEC applicable at $p=2$. Our approach utilizes a weighted version of a conditional $L_p$ norm which extrapolates the quantum expansion/ant-quantity. We elucidate some properties of the corresponding weighted conditional entropy both for half-sided modular inclusions and for general von Neumann subalgebras with a common cyclic and separating vector. The $p=2$ limit computes a conditional dynamical entropy originally defined in the context of black hole dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Faulkner

item.title: Proof of the QNEC, without assumptions and under a weight
item.description: arXiv:2611.11920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We complete a proof of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) in the mathematical framework of Half-Sided Translations and Modular Inclusions (HST/HSMI) removing an assumption that applied to previous proofs. Here we establish a theorem, which when translated to a physical setting implies that the relative entropy comparing the state of fields outside a stationary black hole with a Hartle-Hawking (HH) state is always a convex function of the horizon cut. Previous proofs only applied when a purification with finite null energy was available. We also obtain a QNEC generalization in which the HH Hilbert space is replaced with one based on a weight which is plausibly of relevance to evaporating black holes in flat space.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Faulkner

item.title: Khintchine's limit theorem for monotone convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.11968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every weak limit of monotone convolution powers is monotonically infinitely divisible. In contrast, we prove that every probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ can occur as a weak limit of monotone convolutions of an infinitesimal triangular array. We also discuss similar limit theorems for multiplicative monotone convolution on the unit circle.
item.dc:creator: Cheng-Xuan Soong, Takahiro Hasebe

item.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.12785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations. We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Collins, Yu Kitagawa, Akihiro Miyagawa, Wangjun Yuan, Ping Zhong

item.title: An Eilenberg-Watts Theorem and Morita localization for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2305.10859v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hilbert modules over a $C^*$-category were first defined by Mitchener, who also proved that they form a $C^*$-category. An Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-algebras was proved by Blecher. We follow a similar path to prove an Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories and characterize equivalences of categories of Hilbert modules as being given by tensoring with imprimitivity bimodules. We employ our results to prove several equivalences of bicategories of $C^*$-algebras and $C^*$-categories, and to exhibit a Morita localization of the category of locally small $C^*$-categories.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Pander Maat

item.title: Generic classification of the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2509.00829v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article we show that the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$ are generically classifiable by the inverse temperature of their unique KMS state. Along the way, we show that a large class of quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_n$ are generically equivariantly $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and their corresponding dual action has the Rokhlin property generically.
item.dc:creator: Robert Neagu

item.title: $L_p$-spaces, $1\leq p\ne 2<\infty$, associated with type III and semifinite von Neumann algebras are not isomorphic
item.description: arXiv:2610.11055v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be a type III von Neumann algebra, and let $N$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra. We prove that the Banach space $M_*$ does not embed isomorphically into the Banach space $N_*$. More generally, we prove that $L_p(M)$ is not isomorphic to a subspace of $L_p(N)$ for $1\le p<2$. In particular, the Banach isomorphism class of $L_p(M)$ distinguishes type III algebras from semifinite algebras for $1\le p<\infty$, $p\ne2$. This answers several long-standing open questions in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang, Fedor Sukochev

item.title: Classification of reduced free products of nuclear C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.36459v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider the countably infinite reduced free product $D$ of copies of $(\mathrm C([0,1]),\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure. It is proved that finite and countable reduced free products of unital separable nuclear UCT $\mathrm C^*$-algebras with respect to a chosen family of faithful traces are classified, after adjoining $D$, by the Elliott invariant. In other words, an isomorphism between the naive K-theory invariants of two such algebras is induced by an isomorphism between the algebras.
item.dc:creator: George A. Elliott, Chun Guang Li, Zhuang Niu

item.title: The Douglas property for multiplier algebras of operators
item.description: arXiv:1107.0980v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a collection of reproducing kernels k which includes those for the Hardy space of the polydisk and ball and for the Bergman space, k is a complete Pick kernel if and only if the multiplier algebra of the Hilbert space H^2(k) associated to k has the Douglas property. Consequences for solving the operator equation AX=Y are examined.
item.dc:creator: Scott McCullough, Tavan T. Trent

item.title: The Brown measure of a sum of two free nonselfadjoint random variables, one of which is R-diagonal
item.description: arXiv:2209.12379v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are two $*$-free, possibly unbounded, random variables with Brown measures $\mu_{X_1}$ and $\mu_{X_2}$ respectively. Using properties of classic free additive convolution, we develop a method for calculating $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ when $X_2$ is $R$-diagonal. This method determines a density relative to Lebesgue measure on an open set whose closure equals the support of $\mu_{X_{1}+X_{2}}$. We prove that $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ has no singular continuous part, that its density is strictly positive on this open set, and we determine the masses of its atoms. Explicit calculations are possible in several important cases. As an application, we combine our Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula with known subordination convergence results to calculate the limiting logarithmic potentials of free multiplicative random walks. We identify the limit with the Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula for free multiplicative Brownian motion previously proved by some PDE methods.
item.dc:creator: Hari Bercovici, Yu Kitagawa, Ping Zhong

item.title: Global structure behind pointwise equivalences of noncommutative polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2505.07469v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the interplay between local and global equivalences on noncommutative polynomials, the elements of the free algebra. When the latter are viewed as functions in several matrix variables, a local equivalence of noncommutative polynomials refers to their values sharing a common feature point-wise on matrix tuples of all dimensions, such as rank-equivalence (values have the same ranks), isospectrality (values have the same spectrum), and pointwise similarity (values are similar). On the other hand, a global equivalence refers to a ring-theoretic relation within the free algebra, such as stable association or (elementary) intertwinedness. This paper identifies the most ubiquitous pairs of local and global equivalences. Namely, rank-equivalence coincides with stable association, isospectrality coincides with both intertwinedness and transitive closure of elementary intertwinedness, and pointwise similarity coincides with equality. Using these characterizations, further results on spectral radii and norms of values of noncommutative polynomials are derived.
item.dc:creator: Eli Shamovich, Jurij Vol\v{c}i\v{c}

item.title: Finite dimensional approximations for Hilbert space operators and applications in Quantum Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2509.03384v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we develop a unified framework for quasidiagonal and F\o lner-type approximations of linear operators on Hilbert spaces. These approximations (originally formulated for bounded operators and operator algebras) involve sequences of non-zero finite rank orthogonal projections that asymptotically commute with the operator -- either in norm (quasidiagonal) or in mean (F\o lner). Such structures guarantee spectral approximation results in terms of their finite sections. We extend this theory to unbounded, densely defined closable operators, establishing a generalization of Halmos' classical result: every closable quasidiagonal operator is a compact perturbation of a closable block-diagonal operator on the same domain. Likewise, we introduce sparse F\o lner sequences and establish an interplay between quasidiagonal approximations and the existence of sparse F\o lner sequences. The theoretical developments are illustrated with explicit examples using different types of weighted shifts and applied to quantum mechanical models, including a detailed treatment of the Weyl algebra and its Schr\"odinger representation.
item.dc:creator: Eva A. Gallardo-Guti\'errez, Fernando Lled\'o, Laura S\'aenz

item.title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
item.description: arXiv:2609.10802v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Franz Luef, Eduard Ortega

item.title: Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.09186v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(\Delta(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $\Delta(\mathfrak{A})$ is $\sigma$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia J. Beltr\'an-Meneu, Jorge Galindo, Enrique Jord\'a
